Nested row cleanup precedes statement cleanup; early returns still execute finally. This classification concerns this catch syntax only and is independent of the previous CloseResource observations.

finding.message: A throw statement in a finally block makes the control flow hard to understand.

reason: BackupStepRepository.java.inspect uses a direct finally to close its already-acquired original JDBC resource once. The nested typed cleanup catch throws only when JdbcResourceFailures.replace selects that original cleanup failure: no primary, or known SQLException primary with unknown Runtime/Error cleanup. Thus this is the approved cleanup competition table, not an unconditional finally throw that masks every body failure. Silently returning after a selected cleanup failure would falsely publish success, while blindly changing to Java TWR would change same-Throwable/fixed-secondary and known-versus-unknown priority. ResultSet precedes Statement and borrowed Connection is not closed.

finding.message: Avoid catching RuntimeException in try-catch block

reason: SchemaHistoryAdmission.java.inspect owns an original ResultSet; this RuntimeException body catch records the identical primary then immediately rethrows it so its owning finally can directly close exactly once and resolve a second failure. Removing the catch would leave primary unrecorded and let a close failure incorrectly replace unknown body identity. This is not broad normalization of provider failures. The retained table is: no primary => original cleanup propagates; known SQL body with unknown cleanup => original cleanup; unknown body => same body with a newly fixed redacted secondary; SQL/SQL => fixed outer SQLException normalization. Same throwable is never added to itself. The outer catch accepts only SQLException; unknown Runtime/NPE/Error never becomes a normal result. Nested row cleanup precedes statement cleanup; early returns still execute finally. This classification concerns this catch syntax only and is independent of the previous CloseResource observations.
